L14: # The CAN Team
L15: 
L16: A cancer diagnosis is often devastating and deeply distressing. At ACCWA, we are not only a centre of medical excellence in veterinary oncology but also a source of unwavering support and compassion for owners and their families. We are dedicated to guiding you through every step of the journey with understanding, empathy, and care.
L17: 
L18: At ACCWA, our core value is that we CAN!
L19: These core values define everything we do. Compassion guides us to provide empathetic, patient-centered care, while Collaboration and Community ensure we work together to support patients and their loved ones. We strive for Advancement in treatments and techniques, uphold the highest standards of Accountability, and embrace Adaptability to meet the ever-changing needs of veterinary oncology.
L20: Through Nurture, we care for the physical and emotional well-being of all (including ourselves), maintaining a culture of Nicety — respect and kindness in every interaction. With a focus on the Next Generation, we are committed to sustainable practices that benefit future pets, families, and the environment. Together, we CAN make a difference
L21: 【11†Image: Dr. Jessica Finlay 】
L22: ## Dr. Jessica Finlay
L23: 
L24: BVSc MVS FANZCVS
L25: 
L26: Registered Specialist in Veterinary Oncology
L27: Founder
L28: 
L29: Jess’ love for animals stems from childhood, spending many hours in paddocks surrounded by dogs, horses and wildlife. The daughter of two medical specialists, it was a natural progression to a career and passion for providing a high level of care in her specialised field.
L30: Jess graduated from the University of Melbourne (BVSc) with first class honours in 2004 and then started her career in mixed practice in Gippsland, Victoria.
L31: After 3 years, she moved to small animal practice in Launceston, Tasmania, where she completed post graduate studies in Medical Oncology as well as a Masters in Veterinary Studies (MVS) through Murdoch University and successfully gained Membership to the Australian and New Zealand College of Veterinary Scientists in Small Animal Internal Medicine (including Oncology).
L32: Jess then moved to Perth in 2012 to commence her residency in Medical Oncology, completing her training in 2014 and successfully passed the Fellowship (FANZCVS) examinations in 2017. Jess has consulted with clients and patients from all over Western Australia, including exotic animals at Perth Zoo.
L33: Jess has authored, co-authored and contributed to numerous peer reviewed research publications and has presented some of this research at national and international veterinary conferences. Jess has continued to provide education to veterinary students, primary care veterinarians and residents.
L34: 
L35: 【12†Image: Dr. Jack Cameron】
L36: ## Dr. Jack Cameron
L37: 
L38: BVSc.
L39: 
L40: 
L41: 
L42: Jack always knew he wanted to be a veterinarian. His passion for veterinary medicine began in his early childhood, growing up in Pāpāmoa, New Zealand, a coastal town where his love for animals and nature thrived. As he grew up, his dedication to animal care strengthened, developing the desire to make a positive impact in their lives.
L43: Jack graduated with a Bachelor of Veterinary Science from Massey University in 2023, where he developed his knowledge to help him to become a compassionate and skilled clinician. In early 2024, Jack made the move to Western Australia to further his career and embrace new challenges in and out of the veterinary world.
L44: His interest in oncology developed while working with Dr, Jess, and he found a particular sense of fulfillment in helping patients and their owners navigate the difficult journey of cancer diagnosis and treatment.
L45: Jack is deeply committed to providing high-quality care to animals facing cancer. He hopes to endure further study in the future to aid his passion for making a difference in the lives of pets and their owners, which continues to drive his work every day.
L46: 
L47: 【13†Image: Indiana Price】
L48: ## Indiana Price
L49: 
L50: BVN RVN.
L51: 
L52: 
L53: 
L54: Originally from New Zealand, Indiana is a dedicated oncology veterinary nurse with a strong commitment to delivering high-quality, fear-free care to every patient she meets. After completing her Diploma in Veterinary Nursing in 2020, she went on to earn her Bachelor’s degree in Veterinary Nursing in 2024. Indiana holds herself to exceptionally high standards, driven by a genuine passion for animal well-being and a deep sense of responsibility toward her patients.
L55: Outside of work, Indiana enjoys spending time with her beloved cat, Monkey, exploring the stunning beaches of Western Australia, reading, and relaxing with a good movie.
L56: 
L57: She feels truly privileged to work in a profession that allows her to make a meaningful difference in the lives of animals and their families. Indiana looks forward to continuing to grow in her field and to providing compassionate, expert care to every patient she encounters.
L58: 
L59: 【14†Image: Leigh Green】
L60: ## Leigh Green
L61: 
L62: RVN
L63: 
L64: 
L65: 
L66: With a passion for patient and owner care that spans both general and referral practices, Leigh has had the privilege of working in a variety of veterinary environments. This includes time in a cat-only practice, where feline care and client education became a key focus.
L67: 
L68: Leigh now works with patients and their owners in a special setting that allows for the delivery of compassion, love, and support to those who need it most.
L69: Outside of work, Leigh spends time with family and enjoys her greatest passion – horses and dressage.
L70: ## Fear Free Veterinary Oncologist
L71: 
L72: Jess is a Fear Free Oncologist. Veterinary professionals with Fear Free Certification are trained to recognise and minimise fear, anxiety and stress on patients. The improved experience for both the patient and their families enhances the journey and can lead to improved outcomes.

L71: # Resources for Referring Patients to Upstate Veterinary Specialties
L72: ### Transferring Appointments to Emergency and Urgent Care:
L73: The emergency service is open to our community for walk-in cases 24 hours a day, seven days a week. To directly transfer a patient to the emergency and urgent care service, please call ahead and speak with one of our doctors to discuss the case and the patient’s needs. Following the phone conversation, please submit our online 【27†emergency and critical care direct transfer form】 and include the previous 12 months of medical records, including lab work and radiographs.
L74: After your patient is discharged, our doctors will follow up with a referral report through our electronic medical records portal within 24 hours.
L75: Specialty services and advanced imaging/diagnostics are not available 24/7. Please contact the specialty department coordinator for stable patients to arrange the earliest available appointment. If you feel your patient needs this level of care, please call and speak with one of our emergency doctors before referring your case.
L76: ### Appointments with a Specialty Service:
L77: To send a referral to one of our specialists, please submit our online 【26†specialty referral form】 with a summary of the case and the previous 12 months of medical records. Please include lab work and radiographs when available. After submitting a referral, please direct your clients to contact our team to schedule their appointment.  Following your client’s appointment, our specialists will send a referral report via our electronic medical records portal within 24 hours.
L78: For more information about our portal, please see the Electronic Medical Records Patient Portal section below.
L79: ### Outpatient Ultrasound:
L80: 
L81: Our Radiology Department currently does not provide outpatient ultrasound services. To receive an ultrasound, the patient must be admitted through our emergency or urgent care services and actively be under the care of a UVS Veterinarian.
L82: Our Radiology Team performs ultrasounds Monday through Friday from 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM. Emergency ultrasounds are scheduled based on patient triage priority and the radiology team’s availability. Ultrasounds are scheduled on the day of, based on availability, and cannot be booked in advance or for future appointments.
L83: ### Telemedicine Consults:
L84: 
L85: Veterinarians are welcome to submit telemedicine consults with any of our specialists. If you would like a telemedicine consult, please contact our hospital at 518-783-3198 and request the department you’d like to consult with.
L86: ### Electronic Medical Records Patient Portal
L87: Upstate Veterinary Specialties utilizes Instinct EMR. All referral reports will be managed through their EMR Portal, Shareville. Shareville is a helpful portal where you can receive updates and access shared patient documents from UVS. Shareville will email check-in/check-out notifications and allow your practice to log into the portal to view our referral reports and more. During a patient’s visit, you will be emailed a unique portal link to access your patient’s medical records.
L88: To learn more, download our 【56†Instinct Shareville User Guide】, which covers the requirements to access patient information, instructions for account setup and using your dashboard, and contact information for technical assistance.
L89: 
L90: 【56†Download Now】
L91: ### Request a Visit from a Specialist:
L92: Strong relationships with our referring partners are a top priority. We are dedicated to supporting local practices and being a valuable resource for the referring community. UVS offers in-person visits from our specialists! We appreciate this opportunity to receive feedback, explore best practices, and continue to build collaborative partnerships. Thank you for choosing UVS as your partners for specialty, urgent, and emergency care. 【57†Request】 a visit from our team.

L87: ## Compassionate, cutting-edge
L88: cancer care for pets
L89: 
L90: At ARC Vets, we understand that a cancer diagnosis can be overwhelming for pet owners. Our dedicated oncology team, overseen by Dr. Patrick Smith, a Registered Specialist in Oncology, is committed to providing compassionate, cutting-edge cancer care. Supported by our oncology nurses led by Bridgid King, we offer a comprehensive range of treatments tailored to your pet’s individual needs. Your pet’s quality of life is always our top priority.
L91: ## Comprehensive
L92: Cancer Care
L93: 
L94: Our dedicated oncology service is based at ARC Central. For clients who prefer to be seen at ARC North, our experienced internal medicine team is available to manage oncology cases, provide ongoing care, and co-ordinate treatment.
L95: ## Advanced Oncology
L96: Treatments & Supportive Care
L97: 
L98: 【29†Image: Arc Vets Pet Owner Cat Sitting On Legs】【29†Image: Arc Vets Pet Owner Cat Sitting On Legs】
L99: 
L100:   * ### Chemotherapy Protocols
L101: We design highly customised chemotherapy protocols tailored to each patient's specific diagnosis and staging, utilising the latest advancements in veterinary oncology to maximise therapeutic efficacy while minimising side effects. Our primary goal is to maintain an exceptional quality of life for your pet throughout their treatment journey.
L102: 
L103:   * ### Surgical Oncology
L104: When tumour removal is required, our oncology team works in direct collaboration with our board-certified surgical specialists to maximise the chances of achieving complete removal while preserving your pet's long-term function and comfort. We use advanced pre-surgical imaging to carefully plan each procedure and a range of pain relief techniques to ensure patient comfort.
L105: 
L106:   * ### Electrochemotherapy (ECT)
L107: We offer electrochemotherapy (ECT), a cutting-edge and minimally invasive treatment that combines brief, localised electrical pulses with chemotherapy to dramatically enhance drug uptake directly within tumour cells. This highly targeted approach is exceptionally effective for controlling specific skin and soft tissue cancers, maximising local treatment power while sparing healthy surrounding tissue and minimising systemic side effects.
L108: 
L109:   * ### Radiation Therapy
L110: Used as a standalone treatment or alongside surgery and chemotherapy, radiation therapy targets tumours with extreme precision to shrink masses, halt progression, and alleviate localised pain. Through a unique and collaborative partnership with a premier human medical facility, we ensure our patients have direct access to world-class radiation technology and advanced planning protocols.
L111: 
L112:   * ### Palliative Care & Pain Management
L113: For pets facing an advanced or terminal cancer diagnosis, our absolute priority shifts to ensuring complete comfort, dignity, and an exceptional quality of life. We provide highly advanced, multimodal pain management, targeted supportive therapies, and empathetic guidance to help families navigate difficult decisions with clarity and peace of mind.
L114: 
L115:   * ## Meet The Team
L116: 
L117:   * ### Patrick Smith
L118: 
L119: BSc BVMS (dist) MRCVS DECVIM (Oncology)
L120: 
L121: Registered Specialist in Oncology
L122: Patrick is a board-certified specialist in small animal oncology, certified by the European College of Veterinary Internal Medicine. He graduated from Murdoch University in 2014, completed an internship at VSG in Auckland, and pursued a Master of Veterinary Medicine combined with a residency in small animal oncology at the University of Glasgow. Patrick became a Diplomate in oncology in 2021 and joined ARC shortly after.
L123: Patrick’s clinical interests lie in the diagnosis and management of feline and canine lymphoma. He is dedicated to expanding treatment options for cancer patients in both referral and general practice settings across New Zealand. Patrick’s
L124: 
L125: compassionate, evidence-based approach prioritizes the quality of life for pets living with cancer.
L126: Patrick has published research on canine lymphoma and quality of life assessments during radiation therapy. He remains involved in clinical work, teaching, and research.
L127: 
L128: Outside of work, Patrick enjoys hiking and exploring the natural beauty of New Zealand with his well-travelled cat, Teddy, who enjoys the sunny New Zealand climate from his luxury catio.

L141:   * ## You Are
L142: Not Alone
L143: 
L144: 【30†Image: Arc Vets Nz Arc Vet Smiling With White Burmilla Cat】【30†Image: Arc Vets Nz Arc Vet Smiling With White Burmilla Cat】
L145: 
L146: In cases where a patient is unable to visit our hospital, our oncologist is available to consult with referring veterinarians remotely, ensuring that every pet receives the specialised care they need.
L147: If your pet hss been diagnosed with cancer, you’re not alone—we’re here to help. To learn more about our oncology services or to schedule a consultation, contact us today.
L148: 
L149: 【23†Talk to our team】
L150: ## Compassionate Approach
L151: to Specialist Care
L152: 
L153:   * ### Specialist Care
L154: 
L155: At ARC Vets, we accept referrals from veterinary clinics throughout New Zealand and provide specialist care in state-of-the-art facilities. We know that specialist visits can be overwhelming, and we’re here to make the entire experience as smooth and supportive as possible.
L156: 
L157:   * ### Before Your Appointment
L158: Once we’ve received your referral, our friendly team will contact you to schedule an appointment with the right specialist. We’ll explain the preparation steps to make sure your visit goes smoothly.
L159: 
L160:   * ### During Your Visit
L161: You and your pet will be welcomed into our purpose-built facility, which features separate areas for dogs and cats to reduce stress. Our specialists will carefully review your pet’s medical history, perform a thorough exam, and discuss a treatment plan that works for both you and your pet.
L162: 
L163:   * ### After Your Appointment
L164: Once your pet is discharged, we’ll check in to monitor their recovery. Remote follow-up appointments may also be an option if your pet’s condition allows. We are here to support you and ensure the best possible care for your pet at every stage.
